title: SAML assertion audience mismatch allowing RBAC policy bypass in Private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Private deployment customers reported that service principals using IdP-initiated SAML single sign-on were able to access resources outside of their assigned RBAC scopes. The immediate symptom was missing or malformed 'aud' (audience) claims in SAML assertions produced by an on-prem IdP connector (edge-case config), which our SAML middleware accepted and then mapped to overly permissive role bindings. Additionally, when requests used aliased KMS keys, some audit events were not emitted to the central audit-forwarder, causing gaps in the timeline.

Impact: Affected customers: two enterprise customers in EMEA (managed private installs) reported unauthorized access to dedicated inference endpoints and incomplete audit trails for those sessions. Business impact: potential data access exposure and non-compliance with audit SLAs. Technical severity: P0 (security and compliance).

Root cause (initial findings):
- The SAML validation layer allowed assertions lacking an explicit 'aud' claim when the IdP connector was configured in legacy compatibility mode. Our downstream RBAC role-mapper relied on presence of 'aud' and defaulted to a tenant-global binding on missing values.
- The KMS integration path that resolves key aliases for private customers had a race condition: when an alias resolution call timed out and retried against a secondary endpoint, the audit-forwarder hook was skipped for performance reasons. That produced missing audit entries for several sessions.

Reproduction notes: Repro steps validated in staging with a simulated IdP that strips the audience field. Steps included: 1) configure private stack with legacy IdP connector; 2) craft SAML response without 'aud' attribute but valid signature; 3) exchange assertion for session token and call inference endpoint; 4) observe role binding resolution and check audit-forwarder logs.
proposed_fix:
1) Harden SAML validation: reject assertions that lack an explicit 'aud' claim. Add a config flag to enable permissive compatibility only behind an operator opt-in (default: strict). 2) Update RBAC mapper to never fallback to tenant-global roles on missing claims; require explicit mapping or fail closed. 3) Fix KMS alias resolution to synchronously emit audit events even on transient retries; add idempotent forwarder semantics so events are reliably recorded. 4) Add a migration script to backfill audit events where possible by correlating key-lookup retries and session times.

Technical changes: modify saml/validator.go (strict audience path), rbac/mapper.go (fail-closed logic), kms/alias_resolver.go (retry path emits audit hook), and audit/forwarder service (idempotent dedupe and backoff).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (hotfix): Build runtime-1.22.3-hotfix with the SAML strict-aud validation and RBAC mapper change. Deploy to a single staging private cluster and run end-to-end tests. Run internal canary against two private customers under a coordinated maintenance window. Phase 2 (wider rollout): Gradually promote patch across affected private regions with traffic shaping and automatic rollback on error budget breaches. Phase 3 (post-release): run audit backfill job with customer opt-in and provide signed attestation to customers.

Fallbacks: If unexpected failures occur, revert to previous runtime and open support case with affected customers; enforce maintenance window and temporary ACLs to block cross-tenant requests while investigating.
qa_checks:
- Unit tests for SAML validator rejecting missing aud.
- Integration tests: simulated IdP responses with/without aud, ensure RBAC mapping denies when aud missing.
- End-to-end: run inference requests in staging private cluster; verify audit-forwarder logs for every session and that key alias resolution emits events.
- Fuzz harness against malformed assertions for the next 72 hours post-deploy.
monitoring_and_alerts: Add two new alerts: 1) SAML-aud-missing-rate > 1% over 1h in private clusters; 2) audit-forwarder event drop rate > 0.1% over 30m. Dashboards: 'Private SSO Integrity' and 'KMS Alias Reliability' panels. Create runbook entry for triage.
rollback_criteria:
- Increase in inference 5xx errors from private clusters > 0.5% vs baseline for 15m.
- New customer-auth regressions reported by Support within 2h of deploy.
- Unexpected audit event loss rate > 0.2% for 30m.
postmortem_actions:
- Schedule 72-hour post-release validation window with customers.
- Complete incident writeup and share with Security and Compliance teams.
- Deliver a configuration scanner that flags legacy IdP connector settings.
- Track follow-ups: ENG-18950 (IdP compatibility docs), ENG-18951 (audit backfill automation).
